## `lr-lightbox`

A modal, full-screen image viewer with prev/next navigation, captions, and pan/zoom delegated to one
stable embedded `<lr-pan-zoom>`. It renders its own dialog panel (not a nested `<lr-dialog>`)
but shares the same overlay infrastructure as `<lr-dialog>`/`<lr-command-palette>` — stacking, focus
trap, Escape/backdrop dismissal, scroll lock, and focus return.

Closing returns focus to the element that held it when the lightbox opened, including an opener the host re-shows only after the close.

A lightbox opened outside an existing native `dialog.showModal()` stays interactive through an internal native modal surface. The host keeps its authored parent, and close vetoes, Escape, and focus return retain their normal behavior.

**Properties:**

- `open: boolean = false` (reflected) — post-render writes run the same cancelable lifecycle as
  `show()`/`hide()`/`close()`. Initial `open` markup is state and emits no lifecycle events.
- `images: readonly LyraLightboxImage[] = []` (attribute: false) —
  `LyraLightboxImage { readonly src: string; readonly alt?: string; readonly caption?: string; readonly thumbnail?: string }`
  (`thumbnail` is the `with-thumbnails` strip image, falling back to `src`).
  Assignment clones/freezes the records and inspects at most 10,000 candidates; malformed records
  are omitted and updates require a new collection assignment. `src` is passed to the embedded
  frame, which runs it through `safeMediaSrc()`. `alt`/`caption` are caller data, never localized.
- `imageSource: LyraLightboxSource | undefined` (attribute: false) — identity-owned
  access to the complete ordered collection, taking precedence over `images` while defined.
  Invalid defined sources show a localized error and retry action; they never fall back to the
  legacy array. Setting `undefined` restores the current `images` input. Reassign the source,
  including the same object, or call a keyless `requestUpdate()` after changing its revision or
  mutable provider state. Unrelated named display updates do not refresh the source. With
  `with-thumbnails`, a separate strip window reads the descriptors of the 15 positions around the
  current one (never the whole collection); a position still loading shows its number.
- `index: number = 0` (reflected) — clamped defensively for rendering and re-synced (emitting
  `lr-index-change`) when the active collection shrinks. In source mode, it retains the requested
  logical index while its descriptor and image load.
- `loop: boolean = false` (reflected) — wraps prev/next past the ends.
- `lightDismiss: boolean = false` (attribute `light-dismiss`) — opt in to backdrop dismissal. Off by default, matching `lr-dialog`.
- `withoutCounter: boolean = false` (attribute `without-counter`, not reflected) — hides the
  visible `[part="counter"]`; the polite position announcement stays active.
  Spoken position updates remain active when the counter is hidden: the shadow
  `[part="live-region"]` is only an `aria-hidden` text mirror, while announcements append to the
  shared light-DOM polite sink. Announcements stay silent when the lightbox or a composed ancestor
  is excluded from the accessibility tree.
- `minZoom: number = 0.5`, `maxZoom: number = 4`, `zoomStep: number = 0.25` (attributes `min-zoom`/
  `max-zoom`/`zoom-step`) — pure pass-throughs to the embedded `<lr-pan-zoom>`, which does the
  normalizing.
- `fit: LyraImageFit = 'actual'` (reflected) — opt-in base sizing policy for the current image,
  using the same `contain`/`width`/`actual` choices as `<lr-image-viewer>`. Lightbox and pan-zoom
  start at the image's natural size for detail inspection. Image-viewer starts at `contain` to
  show the entire image and its annotations. `contain` fits both landscape and tall images inside the stage;
  `width` fills its inline size. CSS recalculates either policy when the stage is resized or a
  delayed image source finishes loading, so navigation and opening do not require consumer timers.
  Fit is the base zoom policy: an explicit user zoom remains until navigation or a reset, and
  changing the theme does not mutate the lightbox's zoom property.
- `accessibleLabel: string | null = null` (attribute `aria-label`) — the dialog's accessible name.
  Blank labels use the localized `lightboxLabel` default.
- `detailsPlacement: 'end' | 'bottom' = 'end'` (attribute `details-placement`) — show the details
  at logical inline-end, moving them below the image when the available inline size is below
  40rem. Set `bottom` to always place the details below the image.

More properties: `withThumbnails` (attribute `with-thumbnails`, default `false`): Shows a strip of
thumbnails for jumping between items in every mode; each uses the item's `thumbnail`, else the
full image (a bounded 15-position window with `imageSource`). `withoutNavigation` (attribute `without-navigation`, default
`false`): Hides the previous/next buttons. Swiping and the arrow keys still navigate. `withoutZoom`
(attribute `without-zoom`, default `false`): Disables zooming and removes the zoom button and the
embedded zoom controls.

**Methods:** promise-based `show()`, `hide()`, and `close(reason?)`, plus `next()`, `previous()`, and
`goTo(index)`. `show()`/`hide()` resolve after the successful rendered transition; a veto resolves
without changing state. `goTo()` ignores a non-finite
index without changing state or emitting `lr-index-change`. A finite fractional index is truncated
toward zero before clamping or loop wrapping, so `lr-index-change.detail.index` is always the
accepted logical integer index, including while a source image is loading; `reason` defaults to
`'api'` and is forwarded as the close event's
detail.

**Full image collections:** `LyraLightboxSource` has `revision` and
`images: LyraIndexedView<LyraSourceRecord<LyraLightboxImage>>`, using the types from
`@aceshooting/lyra-ui/data-sources.js`. The host supplies a nonnegative safe-integer `images.count`
and either synchronous indexed access or asynchronous bounded range reads. Each record supplies
a stable global `key`, canonical nonnegative safe-integer `order`, and image `value`. Keep the view
stable within a revision; publish a new revision and refresh when its contents change. Navigation,
clamping, looping and the localized counter use the full logical count, so first, middle and final
images remain reachable in a million-image host collection without copying it into `images`.
Navigation emits `lr-index-change` after the final logical destination renders, including a loading state for a pending image; direct consumer `index` writes stay event-silent. Source mode adds no new event.

Only the current image loads, after resolving its descriptor. The component retains at most three
descriptors in one-record pages, with one range read physically pending and no neighbour prefetch.
Supplied record and image fields must be own data properties; accessors are rejected without
invocation. Each key, `src`, `alt` and `caption` admits at most 65,536 UTF-16 units; oversized or
malformed values fail visibly instead of being clipped. URLs pass `safeMediaSrc()` before loading.
The host owns provider storage and response allocations; actual image decode/pixel memory belongs
to the browser and is not bounded by the descriptor cache.

Source loading clears the old image/caption, marks the stage busy and leaves logical navigation
available. Descriptor or image-load failure shows localized retry chrome; a valid empty collection
is a separate state. Replacing a source, navigating, refreshing, disconnecting or changing owner
document revokes obsolete work, so a late completion cannot display an old image. The same
pan/zoom frame stays mounted and retains focus. The provider should honor the request's abort
signal; stale-result protection does not make an abort-ignoring provider settle promptly.

**Events:** cancelable `lr-show`, followed by `lr-after-show` once the open panel has rendered and its
enter animation has finished;
conditionally cancelable `lr-hide` (`detail: LyraLightboxHideDetail = { source: Element }`):
cancelable before a requested close, non-cancelable when an open instance unmounts. A requested
close then emits cancelable `lr-close-request` with `{ reason: LyraLightboxCloseReason }`.
An accepted dismissal sets `open = false` and emits non-cancelable `lr-close` with the same reason
object. Use
`lr-close-request` for vetoes and `lr-close` for accepted dismissals.
`lr-after-hide` follows once the exit animation has finished. Both after-events fire straight after
the render under `prefers-reduced-motion` or a zero duration, `show()`/`hide()` resolve with them,
and a transition interrupted by the opposite one emits no after-event. Removal while open cannot be vetoed and reports reason
`unmount`. `lr-index-change` (`detail: { index }`, fired
for internally-driven navigation — a button, a thumbnail, a swipe, a keyboard shortcut, or
`next()`/`previous()`/`goTo()` — and when a shrinking active collection normalizes the index; **not** when a consumer sets
`index` directly); `lr-item-change` (`detail: { index, previousIndex, item, previousItem }`, the
items `null` in data mode) fires alongside `lr-index-change` for the same navigations and, like it,
not when `index` is written directly, open or closed (the same rule as `lr-carousel`'s
`lr-slide-change` for a direct `currentSlide` write; call `goTo()` to change the item and be notified); `lr-zoom-change` (`detail: {
zoom }`) is not emitted by the lightbox itself — it bubbles up composed from the embedded frame.

**Slots:** `actions` — extra toolbar buttons (download/share/delete), rendered in `[part="toolbar"]`
between the counter and the close button. `details` — one reusable panel of rich content for the
current image in `images` or `imageSource` mode. Update the panel on `lr-index-change` and initialize
it for the starting index. If you write `index` directly, update the panel in the same operation.
The panel stays hidden for empty galleries, slotted-item galleries, and while a source image is
loading or has failed. It scrolls when its content exceeds the available space and uses the
localized `details` label when it becomes a keyboard-scrollable region.

```html
<lr-lightbox id="gallery" fit="contain">
  <section slot="details">
    <h2>Photo information</h2>
    <p data-location></p>
  </section>
</lr-lightbox>
<script type="module">
  import '@aceshooting/lyra-ui/components/lr-lightbox.js';

  const photos = [
    { src: '/photos/ridge.jpg', alt: 'View from the ridge', location: 'North Ridge' },
    { src: '/photos/lake.jpg', alt: 'Lake from the trail', location: 'Lake Trail' },
  ];
  const gallery = document.querySelector('#gallery');
  const location = gallery.querySelector('[data-location]');
  const updateDetails = index => {
    location.textContent = photos[index]?.location ?? '';
  };
  gallery.images = photos;
  updateDetails(gallery.index);
  gallery.addEventListener('lr-index-change', event => updateDetails(event.detail.index));
</script>
```

**CSS parts:** `backdrop`, `panel` (`role="dialog"` + `aria-modal="true"` while open; fills the
padded safe area rather than shrink-wrapping), `toolbar`, `counter` (visible localized "Image N of
Total"), `live-region` (an `aria-hidden` shadow text mirror; each post-mount `index` change,
including a consumer-driven one, appends the localized position to the document's shared
`[data-lr-live-region="polite"]` sink; initial mount and reconnect are silent), `actions` (wrapper,
`hidden` when nothing is slotted),
`close-button` (always rendered — unlike `<lr-dialog>`'s, which `without-close-button` removes), `stage`, `frame` (the
embedded `<lr-pan-zoom>`), forwarded aliases `frame-viewport`, `frame-content`, `frame-controls`,
`previous-button`,
`previous-glyph`, `next-button`, `next-glyph`, `caption` (only when the current image has one; its
`id` is the panel's `aria-describedby` target), `details` (scrollable details wrapper),
`source-loading`, `source-error`, and `source-retry`
(the current source image's retry button). `stage` exposes `aria-busy="true"` while source
descriptor or native image loading is pending.

Source loading and error messages use `--lr-lightbox-status-color`, falling back to
`--lr-color-on-strong-overlay`. When the image collection shrinks, a listener for the resulting
`lr-index-change` sees the newly rendered image.

Further CSS parts: `navigation-button`: Both the previous and the next button.
`navigation-button-next`: The same element as `next-button`. `navigation-button-previous`: The same
element as `previous-button`. `scroll-container`: The same element as `stage`. `slide`: The wrapper
around the current image or video. `surface`: The viewer's viewport layer. Only positioned and shown
while open (slotted mode). `thumbnail`: One thumbnail button in the strip. `thumbnail-active`: Added
to the current item's thumbnail. `thumbnails`: The thumbnail strip, rendered only with
`with-thumbnails`. `video`: The current video of a `type="video"` item. `zoom-button`: Toolbar
button that toggles between fitted and zoomed in. Rendered for slotted items only;
`images`/`imageSource` galleries keep the embedded `frame-controls`.

Each slotted `lr-lightbox-item` exposes its own `trigger`, `thumbnail-image`, `play-button` and
`play-glyph` parts, described with the slotted items below.

**Themeable custom properties:** `--lr-lightbox-overlay-color` (default
`var(--lr-color-overlay-strong)` — the backdrop scrim), `--lr-lightbox-control-bg` (default
`var(--lr-color-neutral)`) and `--lr-lightbox-control-color` (default `var(--lr-color-on-neutral)`)
— background/foreground for the counter, caption, and every floating/toolbar icon button; these use
the solid neutral token rather than `--lr-color-surface` because the controls float over arbitrary
photo content.

**Optional peer deps:** none.

**Known gotchas:**

- keyboard navigation is RTL-aware on panel/chrome: Arrow forward/back (mirrored under `rtl`),
  `Home`, `End`. When the embedded pan/zoom viewport owns focus, those keys remain with its native
  scroll surface and never change gallery item; `+`/`-`/`0` remain its zoom shortcuts.
- initial focus deliberately goes to `close-button`, not the first tabbable element — a slotted
  `actions` button placed before it does not steal focus.
- zoom/pan reset on navigation is imperative (`resetView()` from `updated()`), not a binding; the
  frame element is reused across navigations rather than recreated, so a keyboard user who tabbed
  into the viewport keeps focus.
- fit sizing is CSS-driven inside the stable frame. The rendered DOM image is not copied or
  measured by the lightbox, so stale load events cannot apply a previous image's size. The fit
  policy covers the painted image only; the lightbox's DOM caption, toolbar, legend-like actions,
  and tooltip content remain outside that image surface.
- scope: no dot indicators, no click-image-to-navigate and no inertial fling (only the release
  distance decides a swipe). Per-item custom content uses `<lr-lightbox-item>` templates (below).

Set `--lr-lightbox-control-hover-bg` and `--lr-lightbox-control-hover-color` for hovered controls. Set `--lr-lightbox-control-active-bg` and `--lr-lightbox-control-active-color` for pressed controls.

### `lr-lightbox` slotted items (`lr-lightbox-item`)

`<lr-lightbox>` also accepts `<lr-lightbox-item>` children (any depth, no nested lightbox), mirroring
`wa-lightbox`/`wa-lightbox-item`. `images`/`imageSource` keep working unchanged and take precedence
when set. With items the host stays inline and the viewer opens over the page.

```html
<lr-lightbox label="Trip" with-thumbnails>
  <lr-lightbox-item src="/photos/a-full.jpg" alt="Harbour" width="1600" height="900">
    <img src="/photos/a-thumb.jpg" alt="Harbour" />
    <span slot="caption">Harbour at dawn</span>
  </lr-lightbox-item>
  <lr-lightbox-item type="video" src="/clips/b.mp4" thumbnail="/clips/b.jpg" alt="Boat"></lr-lightbox-item>
</lr-lightbox>
```

**`lr-lightbox-item`** — `type: 'image' | 'video' = 'image'` (reflected; video shows a play button),
`src` (the link target, so the gallery works without JavaScript and can be opened in a new tab; a modified
click is left to the browser), `srcset`/`sizes` (the lightbox loads the smallest candidate covering
the viewport or a single `px`/`vw` `sizes` length, else the largest), `alt` (defaults to the slotted
`img` alt), `caption`, `thumbnail` (strip image and the item's own image when nothing is slotted),
`width`/`height` (reserve space). Slots: default thumbnail, `caption` (text shown in the viewer),
`play-icon`. Parts: `trigger`, `thumbnail-image`, `play-button`. The `data-active` attribute marks the
current item while open. URLs are validated: `src` for the link with `safeLinkHref()` and all media
with `safeMediaSrc()`; a rejected `src` leaves a button-style trigger and the item out of the viewer.
An item with no `src` is activated with Enter/Space.

**Custom slides** — anything other than an image or a native video (an embed, a player, another
component) goes in a `<template>` that is a direct child of the item. The lightbox copies the
template's content only while that slide is shown, into a `<div slot="slide-content">` it appends to
itself (light DOM, so page styles apply), and removes the copy on any other slide or once the close
motion ends. `src` is optional (it stays the no-JavaScript link when set); `width`/`height` give the
slide its proportions; custom content cannot be zoomed; the slotted `img` or `thumbnail` stays the
page and strip thumbnail. Slotted controls in the copy keep their arrow keys, and content that
handles its own dragging should call `preventDefault()` on `pointerdown` so no swipe starts there.

```html
<lr-lightbox-item width="1600" height="900" thumbnail="/maps/route-thumb.jpg" alt="Route map">
  <template><iframe src="https://maps.example/embed/route" title="Route map" style="inline-size: 100%; block-size: 100%; border: 0"></iframe></template>
</lr-lightbox-item>
```

**Lightbox additions** — `with-thumbnails` (thumbnail strip, in every mode), `without-navigation`
(hides previous/next; arrow keys and swipe stay), `without-zoom` (no zoom button/controls; the toolbar zoom button exists for slotted items only), `label`
(reflected; names the dialog; a host `aria-label` wins), `items` and `currentItem` getters, `zoomIn()`/`zoomOut()`.
`lr-item-change` fires with every `lr-index-change` and adds `{ index, previousIndex, item, previousItem }`
(items are `null` in data mode); like `lr-index-change` it is not fired when `index` is written directly.
Touch and pen swipes (never mouse) follow the pointer once the drag is clearly horizontal: releasing
at least 50px toward an existing item moves to it, the incoming slide continuing from the release
point; a shorter or mostly vertical drag, a drag past the first/last item without `loop` (followed
with resistance) and `pointercancel` settle the slide back. Directions reverse under RTL; under
`prefers-reduced-motion` the slide does not follow the pointer and the release navigates or stays
without motion. No swipe starts on a control, link, video or form field, or while zoomed. A `type="video"` item plays in a native `<video>`
that pauses on slide change and close; zoom is unavailable for video. Slots `close-icon`,
`previous-icon`, `next-icon`, `zoom-in-icon`, `zoom-out-icon`. Added part aliases: `dialog` (panel),
`scroll-container` (stage), `image` (the zoomable `frame`),
`navigation-button`/`navigation-button-previous`/`navigation-button-next`, plus `surface`, `slide`, `video`, `zoom-button`, `thumbnails`, `thumbnail`, `thumbnail-active`.
Match them with `[part~="…"]` when querying.
Motion: `--show-duration`/`--hide-duration` (or `--lr-lightbox-panel-duration`, default
`--lr-duration-base`) drive the open/close and slide animations, which are flattened under
`prefers-reduced-motion`; `lr-after-show`/`lr-after-hide` wait for the open/close motion to finish
(the host stays painted with `data-closing` until the exit motion ends).
`--slide-gap` (`--lr-lightbox-slide-gap`), `--thumbnail-size` (`--lr-lightbox-thumbnail-size`) and
`--media-border-radius` (`--lr-lightbox-media-radius`) style slides and the strip.
Upstream-named styling properties: `--backdrop-color` (scrim), `--backdrop-filter` (default `none`,
e.g. `blur(1rem)`), `--controls-background` and `--controls-color` (controls, counter, caption) and
`--spacing` (gap between toolbar, media, caption and strip; default `var(--lr-space-s)`); each
`--lr-lightbox-*` token wins over its alias. Custom states: `lr-lightbox:state(open)`,
`:state(zoomed)`; on items `lr-lightbox-item:state(active)` (current item while open),
`:state(empty)` (nothing slotted, no `thumbnail`; hidden on the page) and `:state(morphing)` (while
the open/close motion runs for that item).

**CSS parts:** `trigger` (the link, or button-like anchor, that wraps the thumbnail and opens the
lightbox), `thumbnail-image` (the image rendered from `thumbnail` when nothing is slotted),
`play-button` (the play button shown over a video's thumbnail) and `play-glyph` (the default play
glyph inside the `play-icon` slot).
